entries.note: Vendor certificate of analysis (via search snippet). DLS includes hydration/electrokinetic layer and intensity weighting bias, so this is an upper bound on the TA shell. Not peer-reviewed.

entries.conditions: organic-coated Ag NPs 5-80 nm in 1 mM NaHCO3, pH 8, room temperature (in water, coated)
entries.citation: Ma, R.; Levard, C.; Marinakos, S. M.; Cheng, Y.; Liu, J.; Michel, F. M.; Brown, G. E.; Lowry, G. V., Size-Controlled Dissolution of Organic-Coated Silver Nanoparticles, Environ. Sci. Technol. 46, 752-759 (2012)
entries.note: Abstract: 'surface tension of Ag NPs ~1 J/m2' from Kelvin fit; this is the Gibbs-Thomson-relevant interfacial energy of a coated particle in water. Uncertainty is a judgement value.

entries.conditions: 3-mercapto-1-propanesulfonate exchanging citrate on colloidal Au NPs in water; -46 kJ/mol; coverage ~3.5 umol/m2
entries.citation: Dinkel, R.; Braunschweig, B.; Peukert, W., Fast and Slow Ligand Exchange at the Surface of Colloidal Gold Nanoparticles, J. Phys. Chem. C 120, 1673-1682 (2016)
entries.note: Gibbs free energy in water (solution standard state). A thiolate displaces citrate, so citrate's dG must be less negative: upper bound (in magnitude) for citrate. 49% of MPS on edge sites.

entries.conditions: MPS on 5 nm citrate- and NaBr-stabilised Au NPs in water; ca. -40 kJ/mol; only ~2/3 ML MPS on citrate-AuNP
entries.citation: Dinkel, R.; Jakobi, J.; Ziefuss, A. R.; Barcikowski, S.; Braunschweig, B.; Peukert, W., Role of Citrate and NaBr at the Surface of Colloidal Gold Nanoparticles during Functionalization, J. Phys. Chem. C 122, 27383-27391 (2018)
entries.note: Citrate partially resists displacement by MPS (2/3 ML), i.e. citrate dG is not far below the thiolate's: citrate ~ -0.3 to -0.4 eV in water is consistent.

entries.note: Simulator default for the citrate shell. Dense layer only; the solvated/hydrodynamic shell (Cardenas Lopez 2022) is thicker.

entries.conditions: pairs of decahedral Au nanoparticles (few nm) on a support, room temperature
entries.citation: T. H. Lim, D. McCarthy, S. C. Hendy, K. J. Stevens, S. A. Brown, R. D. Tilley, Real-time TEM and kinetic Monte Carlo studies of the coalescence of decahedral gold nanoparticles, ACS Nano 3, 3809-3813 (2009)
entries.note: Qualitative: neck growth between faceted Au particles proceeds over observable (s-min) times and follows atomistic KMC, not continuum (Herring/Nichols-Mullins) sintering, because of faceting. Supports a size-limited coalescence (dmax of a few nm) rather than the d^4 extrapolation. DOI not checked.

entries.conditions: polyacrylate-stabilised Ag nanoparticles destabilised by oppositely charged polyelectrolyte / anions, room temperature
entries.citation: S. Magdassi, M. Grouchko, O. Berezin, A. Kamyshny, Triggering the sintering of silver nanoparticles at room temperature, ACS Nano 4, 1943-1948 (2010)
entries.note: Qualitative: once the stabiliser is removed, Ag nanoparticles (tens of nm) neck and coalesce spontaneously at room temperature, faster than the EAM-u3 Ag dimers in this study suggest. Argues against setting the Ag coalescence cutoff far below Au. DOI not checked.
